name: FL-23
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans Democratic by nine points on partisanship
Frankel holds a huge money edge: $2.3M raised and $1.2M on hand versus $163K for Adeimy
Prediction markets price Democratic win chances at 96-97%
No public general-election polling exists for this race
model.rationale: The district's nine-point Democratic lean, Frankel's roughly fourteen-to-one fundraising advantage, and markets pricing her win odds at 96-97% all point to a comfortable incumbent victory, so the forecast stays near a twenty-point Democratic margin.
model.watch: Any late polling or a surge of outside Republican spending showing Adeimy competitive would be the first real signal that this race is closer than fundamentals suggest.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Lois Frankel, a Democratic incumbent first elected in 2012, is seeking another term in a South Florida district that leans Democratic by nine points. Her Republican challenger, Deborah Adeimy, has raised about $163,000 and had roughly $34,000 on hand, while Frankel has raised $2.3 million and holds $1.2 million in cash. Outside groups have spent modestly to support Frankel and nothing against her.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Frankel's win probability at 96 to 97 percent. With a favorable district, a well-funded incumbent, and no visible challenger momentum, the seat sits firmly in the Safe Democratic column heading into November.
